title: ESP Atlas Firmware
description: A flashable ESP32 firmware project. First-class entity like `brand`: never indexed into the queryable parts table, never a /search or /wizard result. See SPEC-wizard.md.

popularity.description: OPTIONAL dated popularity snapshot (SPEC-firmware-floor.md): GitHub `stars` + `forks`, plus `downloads` (a launcher/M5Burner install count) at author time, plus `editorial_home` (the independent, non-github.com/*.github.io homepage URL that cleared the third floor signal at admission, if that signal is what admitted this record), plus the `as_of` YYYY-MM-DD snapshot date. Stored so the CI floor gate (scripts/firmware_floor_audit.py --ci) and the live PR/G2 guards can enforce the popularity floor without a live fetch (clears on stars OR forks OR an independent editorial home OR downloads >= DOWNLOAD_FLOOR). Dated because popularity drifts and is refreshable. `downloads` was REMOVED 2026-09-04 (self-reported by a third-party catalog, not citable) and RESTORED 2026-10-06 as a qualifying fourth signal: a high launcher/M5Burner download count is proof of real community use that a stars-only bar misses (the M5Launcher/Evil-Cardputer/Doom-for-Cardputer class — tens of thousands of installs, 1 GitHub star), and the 2000-download threshold resists trivial gaming. `editorial_home` was ADDED 2026-10-08: the admit path (jr/drain.py, jr/stage_admit.py) always checked a live homepage, but the offline audit could not see it (not in this schema), so an editorial-home-only admission reliably failed the next offline gate and was discarded forever — stamping the URL here closes that drift. additionalProperties is false here, so any OTHER field reintroduced fails validation rather than drifting back.

benefits_from.description: OPTIONAL soft/UX capabilities the firmware benefits from beyond its hard `capabilities` -- a closed vocab of things a board's own structured fields can prove: an onboard `display`, a microSD in `extras` (`storage`), `power.battery_connector`, native `usb`, or a `gps` module in `extras`. Never a hard requirement; run_guide reasons about presence/absence to teach fit, never to gate it.

requires.description: OPTIONAL, grounded requirement-rationale: hard capabilities this firmware needs and WHY, authored verbatim by the maintainer/dataset author. `board_signal` names the structured board field run_guide checks to state met/unmet for a given board (see esp_atlas_core.run_guide's signal matchers), or is `null` when the capability cannot be proven or disproven from any board's structured record (e.g. sub-GHz radio, NFC, IR) -- taught as a need, never asserted met/unmet.

not_required.description: OPTIONAL, grounded rationale for a capability this firmware explicitly does NOT need (e.g. PSRAM) -- authored verbatim, never a gate, only a teaching point run_guide surfaces regardless of what a given board happens to carry.

socs.description: SoC families the project builds for

summary.description: OPTIONAL grounded one-to-two sentence English synopsis of the README, derived ONLY from the README text by jr/groq_enrich.py's enrich_readme(). Cited via a `field: summary` sources[] entry.

seo_title.description: OPTIONAL per-record override of the SERP <title> (apps/web/lib/format.ts firmwareMetaTitle()), for the rare high-demand page where the generic 'flash guide' formula buries the identity people actually search for. Authored editorial copy, not grounded from a source -- no sources[] entry required. Render-time clamps to TITLE_MAX (60 chars) at a word boundary if the author's string overflows.

readme_lang.description: OPTIONAL ISO 639-1 (or 639-2) language code of the fetched README -- 'en' when it is already English. Accompanies `summary`.

readme_sha.description: OPTIONAL sha256 hex digest of the README text last enriched -- lets jr/backfill_summary.py skip a re-run's Groq call when the README is unchanged. When `readme_lang` isn't 'en', data/firmware/<id>/readme.en.md carries the cached English translation.
